questions.title: 55. What does useTransition do?
questions.summary:
◦ useTransition marks eligible updates as non-urgent.
◦ Keeps urgent UI interactions responsive during expensive rendering.
questions.answer:
◦ useTransition = R^ H^ for marking certain updates as non-urgent.
◦ Returns [isPending, startTransition].
◦ startTransition marks eligible state updates as transition work.
◦ Urgent updates, such as typing, can take priority.
◦ Transition rendering may be interrupted or restarted.
◦ isPending indicates whether transition work remains pending.
◦ Useful for expensive UI updates that should not block immediate feedback.
questions.underTheHood:
◦ startTransition marks updates with transition priority.
◦ R^ associates scheduled work w1 transition lanes.
◦ Scheduler coordinates rendering according to priority.
◦ Higher-priority updates can interrupt transition rendering.
◦ R^ resumes or restarts work as needed.
◦ Completed work is applied during commit.
◦ This does not move JavaScript execution to another thread.
pitfalls: ◦ Transition updates must not directly control text inputs.
◦ Expensive synchronous F() execution still blocks the JS thread.
◦ Transition priority does not guarantee a fixed completion time.
◦ State updates after await may require another startTransition.
followUps: ◦ What is urgent vs non-urgent work?
◦ Why should text input updates remain urgent?
questions.recall:
◦ useTransition → [isPending, startTransition].
◦ Urgent > Transition.
◦ Lanes → Priority → Interruptible r().
◦ Non-urgent UI update ≠ Background thread.
